## The copy-paste problem {.section-divider}

Run analysis → copy number → paste into Word → format table

. . .

Then the data change. And they always change.

::: {.notes}
⏱️ 3 min. Ask: who has had to redo a table because two duplicates were found
late? Every hand goes up.
:::

## Three ingredients

````markdown
---
title: "Knowledge gain"
format: html          <- 1. YAML: metadata
---

## Background         <- 2. Markdown: prose

The flipped classroom...

```{{r}}               <- 3. Chunks: code
mean(students$gain, na.rm = TRUE)
```
````

## Markdown in 90 seconds

| Write | Get |
|---|---|
| `## Methods` | Heading |
| `**bold**` `*italic*` | **bold** *italic* |
| `- item` | Bullet |
| `[text](url)` | Link |
| `@fig-gain` | Cross-reference |

Blank lines matter.

## Chunk options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `echo: false` | Hide code, show result |
| `include: false` | Run, show nothing |
| `eval: false` | Show, don't run |
| `fig-cap:` | Caption |
| `label: fig-x` | Cross-referenceable |

Set defaults once in the YAML.

## The actual magic

```markdown
Mean gain was `r knitr::inline_expr("round(mean(students$gain, na.rm = TRUE), 1)")` points.
```

. . .

> Mean gain was 9.8 points.

. . .

That number is **computed**, not typed. Fix a data error → the sentence
corrects itself.

::: {.notes}
🎯 If they take one thing from this session, it is inline code. Demo it live:
change a value, re-render, watch the sentence change.
:::

## One source, many outputs

```yaml
format:
  html:  {toc: true}
  docx:  {reference-doc: template.docx}
  pdf:   {documentclass: article}
  revealjs: {slide-level: 2}
```

These slides and the workshop website are the same machinery.
